description: Library of impossibilities — every killed invention with reusable lessons.
ceo_directive: Eventually the system should possess a library of impossibilities. That could become one of the strongest parts of the entire invention engine.

entries.mechanism_name: Hydraulic state estimation via impedance spectroscopy
entries.what_was_proposed: Estimate 7 hydraulic states (flow, pressure, obstruction, etc.) from impedance measurements at the eShunt surface.
entries.why_it_failed: Structural identifiability proven (Jacobian rank=7), but NUMERICAL non-identifiability under realistic noise (0.5%). Only 1/7 states recoverable. Condition number 1.88e5, parameter correlations >0.95.
entries.reusable_lesson: If the measurement Jacobian is ill-conditioned (>1e4), the system is numerically non-identifiable even if structurally identifiable. Always check condition number AND rank.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose state estimation from collinear measurements without first checking the condition number and noise sensitivity.
entries.physical_constraint: 7 hydraulic states cannot be recovered from impedance measurements under 0.5% noise. The information content of the measurement is insufficient.

entries.mechanism_name: Multi-mechanism retention (size-selective + hydrodynamic)
entries.what_was_proposed: Combine size-selective membrane with hydrodynamic flow restriction to retain all therapeutic classes.
entries.why_it_failed: Multi-mechanism is Pareto-DOMINATED by hydrodynamic alone for small payloads. Adds engineering complexity without retention benefit for 2 of 3 payload classes.
entries.reusable_lesson: Always compare against the BEST SINGLE mechanism per payload class. A combined mechanism must DOMINATE all singles, not just be 'different'.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose multi-mechanism architectures without proving Pareto-dominance over each single mechanism.

entries.mechanism_name: Large-payload size-selective retention (MWCO membrane)
entries.what_was_proposed: Use a 30kDa MWCO membrane to retain large therapeutics (antibody, gene vector, nanoparticle) while CSF drains.
entries.why_it_failed: CSF turnover rate is 2.88x/day. Over 90 days = 259 complete turnovers. Even with 95% retention per pass, therapeutic is washed out: (0.95)^259 ≈ 0. V1's 0.488 retention was a model artifact.
entries.reusable_lesson: Before investing in any retention mechanism, check the CSF TURNOVER RATE. The turnover rate (2.88x/day) is a physiological constant that makes long-term retention physically impossible for any membrane-based mechanism.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose membrane-based or affinity-based retention for >90 day duration. The CSF turnover rate makes it physically impossible.
entries.physical_constraint: CSF turnover rate = 2.88x/day = 259 turnovers in 90 days. No membrane or affinity mechanism can overcome this. The ceiling is PHYSIOLOGICAL (CSF production rate is a constant).

entries.mechanism_name: Derivative and predictive controllers for venous-aware regulation
entries.what_was_proposed: Use ICP derivative (L3d) or predictive model (L5) to regulate drainage based on venous pressure changes.
entries.why_it_failed: L3d: 9.9% M2 reduction vs 15% threshold. L5: 0% M4 reduction. Both mechanisms failed pre-registered buyer boundaries.
entries.reusable_lesson: Derivative-based controllers are too sensitive to noise. Predictive models require accurate forward models that don't exist for CSF dynamics.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose derivative-based or predictive controllers without first proving the signal-to-noise ratio is sufficient.

entries.mechanism_name: FDVBZ flow-diverting anti-fouling
entries.what_was_proposed: Flow-diverting design to prevent thrombus/fouling accumulation.
entries.why_it_failed: Defeated by El-Shafei retrograde flow on thrombus robustness (5.4x vs NEVER threshold). Retrograde flow can dislodge thrombus → embolization.
entries.reusable_lesson: Any anti-fouling mechanism that relies on flow direction must be tested against RETROGRADE flow. Retrograde flow is a realistic clinical scenario (cough, Valsalva, venous pressure changes).
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose flow-direction-dependent anti-fouling without testing retrograde flow robustness.

entries.mechanism_name: M3_REFINED electrothermal SMA retrieval
entries.what_was_proposed: Electrothermal SMA phase-transition activation for shunt retrieval, with thermal isolation and self-test fallback.
entries.why_it_failed: Three independent failure modes: (1) thermal window narrows to 3°C with isolation degradation, (2) sensor electronics SPOF 8% invisible even with dual redundancy, (3) adhesion ceiling 28% failure is biological. V6's 96.97% AVERAGE masked 30% WORST CASE.
entries.reusable_lesson: ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages mask catastrophic failure modes. Thermal activation in a 37°C body environment has a narrow window (37-45°C = 8°C max). Sensor electronics are a SPOF that cannot be fully resolved by redundancy (common-mode failures).
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose thermal activation mechanisms for implantable devices without (a) proving the thermal window is >8°C, (b) resolving sensor SPOF to <5% invisible, (c) addressing adhesion ceiling with non-snare mechanism.

entries.mechanism_name: M5 mechanical anti-trauma flexible neck
entries.what_was_proposed: Flexible (compliant) segment between rigid eShunt body and venous anchoring point to reduce mechanical trauma.
entries.why_it_failed: Problem existence failure (Article XX). Rigid eShunt body is 1890x stiffer than venous wall — vein deforms around shunt, shunt does NOT impose bending stress. M5 solves a HYPOTHETICAL problem. Also introduces kink risk (-5° safety margin) and fatigue embolization.
entries.reusable_lesson: Before optimizing a solution, VERIFY THE PROBLEM EXISTS at the physics level. The IVC filter analogy (cantilevered) does not apply to the eShunt (both-ends-anchored supported beam). A compliant tube deforms around a rigid object, not the other way around.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose compliant/flexible interfaces for both-ends-anchored implants in compliant vessels. The problem (bending trauma) doesn't exist in this geometry. Do not use analogies from cantilevered devices (IVC filters) for supported-beam devices (eShunt).
entries.physical_constraint: Rigid eShunt (EI=1.6e-1) is 1890x stiffer than venous wall (EI=8.4e-5). The vein conforms to the shunt. No bending stress is transmitted.

entries.mechanism_name: M5_REFINED adaptive over-drainage controller (sleep-state + venous pressure)
entries.what_was_proposed: Adaptive drainage controller using ICP + venous pressure sensors to prevent over-drainage during sleep.
entries.why_it_failed: Problem existence undetermined. The eShunt drains subarachnoid→venous sinus (short path, no hydrostatic column, 7 mmHg differential). Over-drainage is siphon-driven in VP shunts; the eShunt may not have a siphon effect. The valve closes at 7 mmHg (above 5 mmHg over-drainage threshold). BUT: device is too new (first-in-human 2021), insufficient clinical data.
entries.reusable_lesson: Do not assume VP shunt problems apply to the eShunt. The eShunt's drainage geometry is fundamentally different (short path, no siphon). Always verify the problem exists for the SPECIFIC device geometry. Over-drainage is siphon-driven; without a hydrostatic column, it may not occur.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose over-drainage prevention mechanisms for the eShunt without first establishing that over-drainage occurs in the eShunt specifically (not just in VP shunts). The eShunt's short drainage path may inherently prevent the siphon effect.
entries.physical_constraint: eShunt normal CSF-venous differential = 7 mmHg. Valve closes at P_venous + P_valve = 2 + 5 = 7 mmHg (upright), above 5 mmHg over-drainage threshold. Without a hydrostatic column, over-drainage may be physically prevented.

entries.mechanism_name: Mechanical snare via catheter (R1)
entries.what_was_proposed: Endovascular catheter with mechanical snare/grasper engages the eShunt and applies traction for removal. No thermal activation, no electronic sensors, no adhesion dependence.
entries.why_it_failed: Tissue ingrowth is the SAME adhesion ceiling as M3. IVC filter retrieval success drops to ~50% at 6 months. Embolization from tissue fragments conflicts with CE-007 zero-embolization. Not novel (FlowTriever/snares established). Poor failure recovery (craniotomy).
entries.reusable_lesson: Changing retrieval ACTIVATION does NOT change retrieval PHYSICS. Any retrieval mechanism for a permanently implanted endovascular anchor faces the same ingrowth ceiling. The problem is not HOW you pull — it is that the anchor is DESIGNED to be ingrown.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose retrieval mechanisms for permanently implanted endovascular anchors without addressing tissue ingrowth. The ingrowth is by design.
entries.physical_constraint: eShunt anchor designed for tissue ingrowth. Retrieval after 6+ months has ~50% success (IVC filter data). Tissue fragments during retrieval conflict with zero-embolization threshold.

entries.mechanism_name: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
entries.what_was_proposed: Retrograde flush from venous side to clear obstruction. eShunt stays in place, no device removal needed.
entries.why_it_failed: Retrograde flush pushes obstruction debris INTO the subarachnoid space (brain). V11.1 quantitative model: 100% particle SAS entry, 970/1000 >10um. V11.2 CORRECTION: USP <788> 9.7x comparison RETRACTED (USP applies to parenteral, not intrathecal). Replaced with analogical evidence: 152 SAH inflammation studies, 33 arachnoiditis studies. CLEARS device (2025) confirms retrograde flush is already known for VP shunts. eShunt venous drainage makes retrograde inherently more dangerous (debris to brain vs peritoneum).
entries.reusable_lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose retrograde flush or debris-mobilizing clearing for eShunt without addressing the brain-ward debris transport. Safe clearing mechanisms must push debris DISTALLY (toward venous system).
entries.physical_constraint: eShunt drains subarachnoid→venous. Retrograde = venous→subarachnoid = debris to brain. 100% of modeled particles enter SAS. Clinical hazard supported by analogy (SAH, arachnoiditis), not direct shunt-debris evidence.

entries.mechanism_name: Magnetic actuated release (R4)
entries.what_was_proposed: eShunt anchor contains magnetic element. External magnetic field (MRI or electromagnet) applies force to disengage anchor.
entries.why_it_failed: MRI compatibility is a GATEKEEPER for neurosurgical implants (hydrocephalus patients need brain MRI). Magnetic element causes premature release, heating, torque, image artifact. Magnetic force at 5-10cm depth (1/r3 decay) is 10-50x less than needed for ingrowth disengagement (0.05-0.1N available vs 1-5N required). Demagnetization ~1%/year. Partial release creates new failure mode.
entries.reusable_lesson: Magnetic actuation is incompatible with neurosurgical implants that must coexist with brain MRI. The 1/r3 force decay makes deep-tissue magnetic actuation fundamentally insufficient. Any mechanism requiring external magnetic actuation for a deep endovascular implant faces both MRI safety and force-distance constraints.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose magnetic actuation for neurosurgical implants requiring MRI compatibility. Do not propose magnetic mechanisms for deep-tissue (>3cm) actuation where 1/r3 force decay makes mechanism insufficient.
entries.physical_constraint: MRI field (1.5-3T) exerts force on magnetic element causing premature release. Force at 5-10cm depth: 0.05-0.1N (available) vs 1-5N (required). 1/r3 distance dependence is a physics constant.

entries.mechanism_name: R2-C3 predictor v1 — pressure-trajectory + phenotype classification for VSS failure-type prediction
entries.what_was_proposed: Use pre-treatment or early post-treatment physiological measurements (CSF opening pressure, venous pressure gradient, pressure trajectory over time) combined with headache phenotype classification to predict which specific failure phenotype (R2-C1/C2/C3/C4/C5) a VSS-stented IIH patient will develop, early enough to change the salvage treatment decision.
entries.why_it_failed: Three independent failures: (1) §103 SERIOUS THREAT — the Hakim self-adjusting-valve family (WO2020086847A1, US20210379344A1) already claims CSF pressure + venous pressure + differential calculation + continuous monitoring (trajectory) + closed-loop valve control + IIH treatment. The proposed 'pressure trajectory → failure-type classifier' uses the SAME measurements for a different analytical purpose. Without a new technical effect, this is 'AI applied to an existing clinical variable.' (2) NO NEW TECHNICAL PRIMITIVE — no genuinely new signal source found. CGRP as a pre-treatment biomarker was tested and found not presently established (conflicting evidence: one negative study, one positive case series). Other candidates (ICHD-3 headache phenotype, multi-site venous distribution, intra-procedural response) are untested with no available data. (3) DECISION-VALUE TEST FAILS — Q2 (earlier-than-routine prediction) = NO (requires post-VSS LP which clinicians already perform); Q3 (improves decision) = UNKNOWN/NEGATIVE (proposed CGRP mAb salvage treatment has conflicting evidence).
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM (sharpened per CEO Round 56o): 'Existing information + existing transformation + existing control, merely recombined, is insufficient. A combination qualifies only if it produces a demonstrably new technical effect that survives prior art and non-obviousness attack. A world-class invention needs a genuinely new technical information source, transformation, or control capability. Do not build an AI layer on top of an already-claimed sensing/control architecture.' NOTE: This theorem does NOT create a universal 'new sensor required' rule. A novel combination of existing measurements CAN qualify if it produces a new, technically non-obvious effect. The theorem rejects TRIVIAL recombination, not all combinations.
what_to_avoid: Do not propose AI classification of physiological variables that are already measured and controlled by existing patent claims (Hakim family).
Do not assume that 'measuring the same thing for a different purpose' constitutes a new technical effect.
Do not propose CGRP as a pre-treatment discriminator without acknowledging the conflicting evidence (2022 negative study vs 2025 positive case series).
Do not propose a salvage treatment pathway without establishing that the salvage treatment itself works (CGRP mAb evidence is conflicting).
evidence_sources: US20040267187A1 / US7318813B2 (Rosenberg/Codman — self-adjusting valve with pressure-over-time)
Lakhani 2026 (PMID 41879313 — symptom phenotype → VSS readmission risk)
Physicians Weekly 2025 (CGRP levels not significant between IIH and controls)
Neurology Live 2022 (CGRP mAbs no significant impact on persistent IIH headache)
entries.cgp_correction: CGRP as the proposed discriminator is NOT PERMANENTLY KILLED. The correct classification is 'not presently established.' A single negative/limited study kills that specific evidentiary basis, not the entire biomarker category. Future evidence may re-open CGRP as a discriminator if: (a) a larger study finds significance, (b) CGRP is combined with other biomarkers, or (c) CGRP is measured in a different compartment (CSF vs serum).

entries.territory_id: CV-T05 (R2-C3 phenotype discovery, Round 56 orthogonal search)
entries.mechanism_name: OSV-4: HRV/autonomic state as orthogonal predictor for R2-C3
entries.what_was_proposed: Use heart rate variability (HRV) as a genuinely orthogonal physiological signal (from the autonomic/cardiac system) to predict R2-C3 phenotype after VSS, on the theory that autonomic dysfunction might identify patients whose headache persists despite ICP normalization.
entries.why_it_failed: Three independent failures: (1) CAUSAL PATHWAY REVERSIBLE — Schmidt 2018 (PMID 29472865, cited 149x) establishes that ICP is a 'REVERSIBLE determinant of efferent sympathetic outflow.' If post-VSS ICP normalizes, sympathetic activity should reverse too. In R2-C3 (ICP already normal), sympathetic activity should already be normal. HRV cannot distinguish R2-C3 (normal ICP + headache) from controls (normal ICP + no headache). (2) PROXY FOR ICP — Schmidt 2018 shows HRV is driven by ICP ('ICP is a determinant of sympathetic activity'). If ICP is already measured (Hakim), HRV is a NOISIER VERSION of ICP, not an independent signal. This is the same pattern as CE-012: 'existing measurement + new purpose.' (3) NO NEW DECISION — if HRV is a proxy for ICP, no new decision is enabled that ICP doesn't already enable.
entries.reusable_lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.
what_to_avoid: Do not assume a signal from a different physiological system is independent just because it uses a different sensor.
Do not propose HRV or autonomic markers as predictors of conditions driven by ICP without first establishing that the autonomic change PERSISTS after ICP normalization.
Do not assume 'orthogonal to one patent' means 'independent of the measured variable.'
entries.physical_constraint: ICP is a reversible determinant of sympathetic activity (Schmidt 2018). HRV reflects ICP-driven sympathetic changes. In the R2-C3 phenotype (ICP normal), HRV should be normal because the driving variable (ICP) is normal.
evidence_sources: Schmidt 2018 (PMID 29472865, Front Physiol) — 'ICP Is a Determinant of Sympathetic Activity'

entries.mechanism_name: RES-4 broad: adaptive cerebrospinal venous stent with sensing + flow regulation
entries.what_was_proposed: Adaptive venous sinus stent with sensor + microprocessor + variable diameter + closed-loop control for dynamic venous outflow regulation in IIH. The broad claim was that 'dynamic venous outflow regulation' is a new technical effect not achievable by shunts or static stents.
entries.why_it_failed: US11304793B2 (priority 2010-02-10, active until 2031) materially occupies the broad architecture. Claim 1 covers: self-expanding stent in cerebrospinal vein + sensor detecting physiological trigger (rising venous backpressure) + microprocessor automatically actuating stent to variable force + deformable constraining member for post-implant tunability + closed-loop (sensor→processor→actuation). The 12-search prior-art attack in Round 56q MISSED this patent because the search used internally coined terminology ('adaptive venous stent', 'sensing stent') rather than the patent's actual language ('cerebrospinal venous insufficiency', 'tunable endovascular device', 'deformable constraining member').
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-014: 'No result for our formulation is not evidence that the capability is absent. Patent searches must generate terminology from patent claims + descriptions + CPC classes + inventor vocabulary + adjacent technologies, not just internally coined phrases. A query-fragile search produces false negatives.' The machine must be better at discovering what competitors actually claimed than it is at inventing elegant names for what we hope is new.
what_to_avoid: Do not conclude 'no prior art found' based on keyword searches using internally coined terminology.
Do not assume that the absence of results for our formulation means the capability is novel.

Future patent searches must include: (a) CPC class traversal, (b) inventor/assignee neighbor search, (c) adjacent technology terminology, (d) backward/forward citation chains, not just keyword matching.
Do not propose 'adaptive stent' or 'sensing stent' architectures without first searching CCSVI/MS patent literature, which uses different vocabulary for the same concepts.
evidence_sources: US11304793B2 (priority 2010-02-10, active 2031) — adaptive cerebrospinal vein stent with sensor + microprocessor + variable expansion
entries.narrow_gap_surviving: The narrow gap (adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for IIH, specifically regulating CSF absorption at the arachnoid granulation site) is NOT killed. US11304793B2 covers IJV (extracranial) for MS, not transverse/sigmoid sinus (intracranial) for IIH. The physiological effect may be different (CSF absorption regulation vs venous return regulation). But §103 risk is SERIOUS (obvious anatomical transfer).

entries.mechanism_name: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
entries.kill_reason: KILLED_UNDER_MODEL_BOUNDED_PHYSICS (insufficient control authority under realistic post-stenting conditions)
entries.what_was_proposed: An adaptive (variable-diameter) venous sinus stent that could regulate CSF absorption by modulating venous pressure at the arachnoid granulation site, producing a technical effect (CSF absorption regulation) that shunts and static stents cannot.
entries.why_it_failed: Physics sensitivity model shows that changing stent diameter by ±2 mm (6mm → 10mm) in a patent venous sinus produces only 0.13-0.19 mmHg change in the AG pressure gradient — far below the pre-registered 1 mmHg kill threshold. Root cause: at venous flow rates (200-500 mL/min), the Poiseuille pressure drop across a 40mm patent segment (6-12mm diameter) is only 0.01-0.2 mmHg. The AG gradient (3-5 mmHg normal, 15-35 mmHg in IIH) is dominated by CSF pressure and downstream venous pressure, NOT by stent diameter. The stent maintains LUMEN PATENCY (prevents collapse), not FLOW REGULATION. Once patent, changing diameter has minimal hemodynamic effect.
entries.reusable_lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.
what_to_avoid: Do not propose adaptive diameter control for patent (non-stenotic) vascular segments without first calculating the Poiseuille pressure drop at the operating flow rate.
Do not assume that r^4 sensitivity at small diameters translates to authority at large diameters — the absolute pressure drop matters, not just the relative change.
Do not propose 'flow regulation' for a device whose physical role is 'patency maintenance' — these are different physical functions.
entries.physical_constraint: At Q=350 mL/min, L=40mm, μ=3.5cP: ΔP across patent 8mm stent = 0.06 mmHg. ΔP across 6mm = 0.19 mmHg. ΔP across 4mm = 0.97 mmHg. The AG gradient (15-35 mmHg in IIH) is 2-3 orders of magnitude larger than the stent pressure drop. Changing diameter from 6→10mm changes AG gradient by only 0.17 mmHg.
evidence_sources: J Physiol 1998: CSF absorption is pressure-driven

model_assumptions.diameter_range: 6-12 mm (patent regime only; stenotic regime excluded)
model_assumptions.flow_range: 200-500 mL/min (published data reports up to 1582 mL/min)
model_assumptions.network_topology: NOT modeled — no collaterals, no contralateral sinus, no flow redistribution
model_assumptions.AG_location: ASSUMED downstream of stent; not mapped to specific AG-bearing regions
model_assumptions.stenotic_regime: EXCLUDED from analysis — circular dismissal (stent operates AT stenosis, not just in patent regime)

entries.correction_note: Downgraded from PROVEN_INVARIANT to MODEL_BOUNDED_NEGATIVE_RESULT per CEO Round 56u directive. The model's assumptions are too narrow to support a universal invariant.

network_model_results.physiological_compatibility: PASSING configs require D≤4mm AND Q≥1200 mL/min — incompatible with stented patient (D=7-10mm, Q=200-500)

entries.engineering_lesson: Diameter control has leverage where resistance is HIGH (small diameter, high flow), not where the vessel is already WIDELY PATENT. Future fluidic inventions must calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point before proposing variable geometry. The useful invention space, if one exists, is unlikely to be 'adaptive diameter control of an already-patent stent.'
entries.ceo_correction: CEO Round 56v: CE-015 is NOT a universal impossibility theorem. It is a model-bounded negative result under specific assumptions. Real cerebral venous drainage is heterogeneous (variable dominance, collateral/epidural drainage). Phase-contrast MRI reports variable sinus flows (434±204 and 195±152 mL/min for R/L TS). The model strongly bounds the candidate but does not prove universal impossibility.

entries.mechanism_name: Stroke: clot-vessel adhesion isolation + measurement + strategy selection (Layer A: force-decomposition estimator v1)
entries.killed_at_version: Round 58 (CEO verdict: kill implementation, not scientific question)
entries.kill_reason: IMPLEMENTATION_KILLED (not universal impossibility). The force-decomposition adhesion estimator v1 is unstable under realistic clot mechanics, and adjacent prior art materially occupies the sensing-and-feedback space. The current Layer-A implementation is KILLED. The scientific question of whether adhesion is measurable by ANY protocol is NOT closed.
entries.what_was_proposed: Three-layer invention: (A) sense clot-vessel adhesion as a distinct force component via controlled perturbation (velocity sweep + relaxation pause), (B) break adhesion with new mechanism, (C) select retrieval strategy based on measured adhesion. Decomposed from: 'Can we know before the first pass which clot-vessel interaction will defeat the planned thrombectomy?'
entries.why_it_failed: Layer A implementation v1 (force decomposition) FAILS under realistic model perturbations: when contact area changes (M3) and adhesion grows with contact time (M4), the constant-tail estimator conflates adhesion growth with slow viscoelastic relaxation. Synthetic ground-truth test under M3+M4 produced +112% bias vs initial adhesion. The Round-57 structural identifiability result was conditional on ideal assumptions (constant adhesion, known contact area, truly static pause). Layer B MATERIALLY OCCUPIED — US11504151B2 (Stryker) claims expandable scraper that dislodges clot from vessel wall with controlled radial force. Layer C MATERIALLY OCCUPIED — US20260000423A1 claims sensor feedback -> therapy mode selection. EP4637580A1 describes force sensing on a thrombus including pulling force and attachment monitoring.
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.
what_to_avoid: Do not propose to measure a specific force component without first testing identifiability
Do not assume causal independence implies measurement identifiability
Do not propose 'select strategy based on measurement' if the measurement cannot be uniquely obtained
Do not assume 'selecting between devices' is patentably distinct from 'selecting between modes of same device' (US20260000423A1)
Do not prove identifiability by choosing the equations that make it identifiable (CEO Round 58 pushing-the-envelope principle)
Do not claim universal non-identifiability from a single unfavorable model — that is the symmetric error to naive identifiability
Do not rescue a killed implementation with v2 / AI classifier / neural-network inference / 'smarter' force decomposition — those are the same idea in a different dress
entries.physical_constraint: BOUNDED, NOT UNIVERSAL. Under the tested M3+M4 realistic model (changing contact area + time-varying adhesion), the constant-tail force-decomposition estimator exhibits +112% bias. This establishes that THIS estimator fails under THIS realistic perturbation model. It does NOT establish that adhesion is fundamentally unmeasurable by any protocol. The 5-component static force equation (F_total = F_adhesion + F_friction + F_drag + F_deformation + F_device_vessel) remains structurally identifiable under the ideal Round-57 model; the failure is model-conditional, not absolute.
evidence_sources: US11504151B2 (Stryker expandable scraper — dislodges clot from vessel wall)
EP4637580A1 (force sensor on thrombus — pulling force + attachment monitoring)
Round 57 formal identifiability analysis (favorable rank under ideal model)
Round 58 adversarial model-uncertainty test (+112% bias under M3+M4 realistic model)
Round 58 synthetic ground-truth test (model-conditional, NOT universal)
entries.retraction_note:
CEO Round 57: original CE-016 'adhesion cannot be identified even with perfect sensors' RETRACTED as too absolute — naive unknown-count is insufficient.
CEO Round 58: the Round-58 claim 'NOT IDENTIFIABLE under realistic physics' is ALSO RETRACTED as too absolute. The +112% bias establishes that the constant-tail estimator fails under the M3+M4 perturbation model chosen by the coder; it does NOT establish universal non-identifiability. The 16-unknowns-vs-3-observables count repeats the Round-56z mistake in elaborate form. The correct bounded statement is: 'The proposed force-decomposition protocol is experimentally/model-wise unstable under realistic clot mechanics, and existing sensing/control prior art substantially occupies adjacent capabilities. The current Layer-A implementation is therefore KILLED.' That is strong enough to close this implementation without claiming a universal impossibility theorem.
entries.stroke_territory_status: Stroke territory is NOT universally exhausted. The recalcitrant-clot problem remains real. ONLY the specific force-decomposition adhesion-isolation + strategy-selection implementation v1 is killed. Other approaches (clot composition imaging, device-clot interaction modeling, pharmacological weakening, alternative sensing modalities) have NOT been explored and remain open.

amendment_history.action: ORIGINAL — claimed universal non-identifiability by naive unknown-count (5 unknowns, <=4 equations)
SHARPENED — required formal rank/observability analysis; built favorable model showing structural identifiability
amendment_history.verdict: Conditional on ideal assumptions; insufficient per CEO Round 58

amendment_history.action: SHARPENED AGAIN — model-uncertainty survival test required. Both directions bounded: one favorable model is not enough; one unfavorable model is not enough. Implementation v1 KILLED; scientific question NOT closed.
amendment_history.verdict: CURRENT — this is the operative version.

entries.territory_id: Cross-cutting (extracted from Stroke Round 58; applies to all latent-variable inventions)
entries.mechanism_name: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
entries.killed_at_version: N/A (this is a theorem, not a killed candidate)
entries.what_was_proposed: Reusable rule: a candidate that depends on measuring or estimating a latent quantity (force component, physiological state, contact property, material parameter) must demonstrate identifiability in TWO layers, not one: (1) structural identifiability under an explicit observation/dynamics model with full rank analysis, AND (2) survival under an adversarial model-uncertainty test where each ideal assumption is relaxed toward realistic physics and identifiability is re-tested under the combined relaxed model. The test must be performed by an agent that is trying to DESTROY identifiability, not preserve it.
entries.why_it_failed: Originated from the Round-57 -> Round-58 sequence on stroke thrombectomy adhesion sensing. Round 57 built a favorable model and showed structural identifiability. Round 58 deliberately relaxed the assumptions (nonlinear friction, viscoelastic Prony relaxation, changing contact area, time-varying adhesion, nonzero velocity during pause, parameter drift) and showed the constant-tail estimator produced +112% bias under M3+M4. The Round-57 result was an artifact of simplified assumptions. The Round-58 result was an artifact of the coder's chosen perturbation model. The asymmetric lesson: BOTH a single favorable model AND a single unfavorable model are insufficient.
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).
what_to_avoid: Do not record 'X is unmeasurable' from a single unfavorable estimator/model pair
Do not record 'X is measurable' from a single favorable rank calculation
Do not rescue a killed implementation with v2 / AI / neural network / 'smarter' classifier — that is the same idea in a different dress
Do not let the coder choose the perturbation model — the model should be chosen adversarially by a separate role
Do not conflate model-conditional failure with mechanism failure (per Article XXIX)
Do not conflate model-conditional success with mechanism success (symmetric error)
entries.physical_constraint: BOUNDED. The +112% bias observed in Round 58 is bounded to: (estimator = constant-tail force decomposition) x (model = M3+M4: changing contact area + time-varying adhesion). Outside this product, no claim is made. This is the operational form of Article XXX (never optimize the evaluator) applied to model-uncertainty testing.
evidence_sources: CEO Round 58 directive: 'A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas.'

entries.territory_id: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
entries.mechanism_name: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
entries.killed_at_version: N/A (this is a theorem, not a killed candidate)
entries.what_was_proposed: Reusable rule: before any novelty claim, the candidate must survive a CAPABILITY collision test against the prior art landscape. The test asks: 'Could a skilled person reconstruct the proposed element from the entire relevant technological neighborhood?' — NOT 'Did anyone use our exact phrase?' The test maps the candidate's capabilities (what it can DO) to prior art capabilities, and requires that at least one capability be genuinely unoccupied (not just reworded).
entries.why_it_failed: Originated from the Round 60/61 → Round 62 sequence. Round 60/61 searched 6 CE-014 vectors using the candidate's own vocabulary ('retrieved-clot physical signature') and found zero blocking prior art. Round 62 CEO audit found 3 direct prior art collisions (US20250186070A1 confirmed P0; US20230062684A1 and EP3763305A1 appear to be mis-citations but do not rescue the candidate) plus Clotild/Sensome commercial frontier, all occupying the broad capability landscape. The Round 60/61 search PASSED on keyword collision but FAILED on capability collision.
entries.reusable_lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT search for your candidate's exact phrase — search for the capability it provides
Do NOT use semantic distinctions ('retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ') as novelty loopholes — this is CE-012 violation
Do NOT conclude novelty from keyword-collision search alone — capability collision is mandatory
Do NOT ignore commercial frontier evidence (Clotild/Sensome) — it occupies capabilities even without a patent
Do NOT assume your search vocabulary matches the prior art's vocabulary — use CE-014 multi-vector multi-vocabulary search on the CAPABILITY, not the candidate
Do NOT claim novelty for an intermediate layer (sensor, feature, algorithm) that plugs into an existing end-to-end system — that is substitution, not invention
Do NOT decompose only to the capability layer — decompose to the complete causal loop (input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome)
Do NOT claim a 'novel prediction' without specifying the exact intervention it enables and the exact measurable outcome that intervention produces
Do NOT pick multiple adverse events to predict — pick exactly ONE and build the complete loop around it
entries.physical_constraint: BOUNDED. The capability collision test is operationally harder than keyword collision test because it requires decomposing the candidate into functional capabilities and searching each against the prior art landscape using the prior art's own vocabulary. But it is the only test that catches the CE-012 failure mode (semantic re-skin of known capability).
evidence_sources: Round 60/61 CE-014 keyword-collision search (found zero blocking prior art)
Round 62 CEO audit (found 3 direct prior art collisions + Clotild/Sensome commercial frontier)
Round 62 capability collision matrix (confirmed Capabilities 1, 2, 5, 7 fully occupied; Caps 6, 8 partially occupied; Caps 3, 4 INCONCLUSIVE)

entries.mechanism_name: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
entries.kill_reason: VALIDATED_NEGATIVE — killer experiment failed twice. R250: 87% assurance, 26% false rejection, dominated by BOED. R251: conformal risk control improved to 97.86% assurance, 4% false rejection, but still failed 3 of 5 pre-registered conditions (assurance <98%, tests >BOED, false reject >BOED). Mechanism core claim (minimum sufficient evidence) not achieved — MSVED selected MORE evidence than BOED while delivering WORSE assurance.
entries.what_was_proposed: Automatically derive the minimum sufficient validation evidence for an ML model modification, proving sufficiency via a 4-link chain from ML change through clinical pathways, risk envelope, to minimum evidence and sufficiency proof.
entries.why_it_failed: The clinical-pathway bridge (link 1) did not produce a smaller evidence set than BOED (information-maximizing selection). MSVED used 16.5 tests vs BOED 15.0. The sufficiency mechanism (min-score in R250, conformal risk control in R251) could not achieve 100% assurance with fewer tests than BOED. The mechanism is WORSE than the BOED baseline on all metrics.
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.
what_to_avoid: Do not claim minimum sufficient evidence without comparing against BOED (information-maximizing selection), not just conventional full-validation.
Do not use union-bound sufficiency rules (min-score for ALL tests) — they are exponentially conservative.
Do not assume the clinical-pathway bridge produces fewer tests — it may produce MORE tests due to pathway-coverage requirements.
Do not propose MSVED-R2 — the pre-registered kill rule was binding.
entries.physical_constraint: The conformal risk control mechanism (R251) improved false rejection from 26% to 4% but could not reduce test count below BOED. The pathway-coverage requirement (selecting tests covering 80% of affected-pathway risk mass) inherently uses more tests than BOED population-level selection.

entries.mechanism_name: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
entries.proposed_version: R249 (discovery) → R251 (§103 conditional) → R252 (theorem + killer + IP)
entries.kill_reason: VALIDATED_NEGATIVE — TWO independent kill signals: (1) Killer test FAIL: system correctly rejects insufficient evidence (E1) but cannot demonstrate correct acceptance of sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification (E2 was rejected because the synthetic modification was genuinely unsafe on P1/P2). (2) IP attack KILL: the MSES theorem is an INTEGRATION of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage argument + Bonferroni correction + sensitivity analysis), not a novel mathematical result. Under KSR v. Teleflex, combining known methods to solve a problem FDA explicitly asks for is likely obvious.
entries.what_was_proposed: A formal mathematical proof that a specific selected evidence set E is sufficient to establish that a model modification Δ remains within a clinical risk envelope R, under frozen assumptions A. Output: E ⊢_A R(Δ), a machine-checkable proof obligation.
entries.why_it_failed: The theorem decomposed into 4 components: (a) per-property NI test (standard, ICH E9), (b) coverage argument (marginal, concept exists in software testing), (c) Bonferroni correction (standard, 1936), (d) assumption-violation analysis (marginal, concept exists). Each component is standard. The integration is engineering, not invention. No novel mathematical bound, no tight bound on minimum evidence size, no proof technique connecting pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency. The killer test also revealed that the system only detects unsafe modifications but cannot certify safe ones — detection is necessary but not sufficient for a sufficiency proof.
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).
what_to_avoid: Do not claim a theorem is novel if it decomposes into standard statistical methods.
Do not confuse integration of known methods with a new mathematical result.
Do not design killer tests with only true-negative cases — include true positives.
Do not assume that machine-checkable = mathematically novel. A JSON proof obligation with standard statistical components is still standard statistics.

r253_correction.correction: R252 kill was based on INVALID POSITIVE CONTROL (E2 contained an unsafe modification). R253 corrected the test cohort, found an implementation bug (NI test used superiority instead of non-inferiority), fixed the bug, and re-ran. Gate A (scientific mechanism) PASSES. Gate B (IP novelty) FAILS. CC-04 is RECLASSIFIED as COMMERCIAL_TOOL_NOT_INVENTION, NOT KILLED.
r253_correction.status: RECLASSIFIED — not a World-Class invention but potentially a commercial tool

entries.mechanism_name: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
entries.kill_reason: VALIDATED_NEGATIVE — §103 obvious. Every component is standard: (1) NI testing (ICH E9, 1998), (2) ML modification context (taught by FDA PCCP guidance Dec 2024), (3) automated reporting (standard in SAS/R/Python), (4) Bonferroni correction (1936), (5) pre-registered margins (standard clinical trial practice). No inventive step. Under KSR v. Teleflex, obvious to try. Killed immediately — no simulation, no killer experiment.
entries.what_was_proposed: Automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins, FDA-grade reporting for ML model modifications under PCCP.
entries.why_it_failed: All 5 components are standard statistical practice. The combination is obvious. FDA PCCP guidance itself teaches the need for NI testing in ML modification context. There is no new mathematical relationship, no new algorithm, no new technical effect.
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.
what_to_avoid: Do not invest in candidates whose own description says "high collision risk".
Do not confuse "least negative EV" with "worth investing in."
Do not automate standard statistical tests and call it an invention.
When all candidates have negative EV, invoke NEW-HUNT MODE — do not grind on the least-bad option.

entries.mechanism_name: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
entries.killed_at_version: R264 (CEO found 5 prior-art sources for the interaction)
entries.kill_reason: VALIDATED_NEGATIVE — synergy without novelty. SGET had genuine functional interaction (synergy score 2) but the interaction itself sits in a crowded neighborhood. CEO found 5 sources: (1) electrochemical impedance depth profiling of tissue (ScienceDirect), (2) vibratory actuator + strain sensor for 1-8mm depth tissue characterization (PubMed 34045731), (3) stretchable electrochemical sensors on mechanically deformed tissue (PubMed 32632992), (4) implantable mechanical+chemical+neural platform (Nature Materials 2026), (5) orthopedic implant mechanical/electrochemical monitoring patent (CN121647794A). The emergent effect (depth-resolved tissue chemistry) already exists via multiple mechanisms.
entries.what_was_proposed: Strain pulse (A) changes electrochemical sensor (B) operating state from steady-state diffusion (2D, 10-100um) to transient forced-convection sampling (3D, 1-10mm). Emergent effect: depth-resolved tissue chemistry from single implant surface.
entries.why_it_failed: Synergy is necessary but not sufficient. The INTERACTION ITSELF must survive prior art. SGET searched for A and B separately but did not search for the interaction law or the emergent effect. The emergent effect (depth-resolved chemistry) already exists via microdialysis, OCT spectroscopy, MRI spectroscopy, and vibratory tissue characterization. The interaction (mechanical+electrochemical tissue sensing) already exists in 5 sources.
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.
what_to_avoid: Do not claim synergy without searching for the INTERACTION ITSELF in prior art.
Do not compare against weak baselines — identify and compare against the STRONGEST existing approach.
Do not assert unexpected effect without quantifying it.
Do not assume A changes B is novel just because A and B are known independently — the interaction may already exist.
